verses.text: Josiah was eight when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.
He did what was right in the LORD’s eyes. He followed the example of his ancestor David without veering right or left.

In his eighth year as king, while he was still young, he started seeking the God of his ancestor David. In his twelfth year, he started clearing out Judah and Jerusalem’s high places, Asherah poles, carved idols, and metal idols.

They tore down the Baals’ altars right in front of him. He cut down the incense altars above them, smashed the Asherah poles and the carved and metal idols, ground them to dust, and scattered it over the graves of those who’d sacrificed to them.
He burned the priests’ bones on their own altars, clearing Judah and Jerusalem of these things.
He did the same among the ruins of the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, all the way to Naphtali.
All across Israel, he tore down the altars, ground the Asherah poles and carved idols to powder, and cut down every incense altar. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

In his eighteenth year as king, after clearing out the land and the temple, Josiah sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city governor, and Joah son of Joahaz, the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They went to Hilkiah the high priest and handed him the money brought into God’s house. The Levite doorkeepers had collected it from Manasseh, Ephraim, all who were left in Israel, all Judah and Benjamin, and the people of Jerusalem.
They handed the money to the people overseeing the work at the LORD’s house, and the workers there used it to fix up the building.
They paid carpenters and builders to buy cut stone, timber for the joints, and beams for the buildings the kings of Judah had let come to ruin.

The men did their work faithfully. Jahath and Obadiah, Levites descended from Merari, directed them along with Zechariah and Meshullam from the Kohathites and other Levites who were all skilled musicians.
They also supervised the people carrying loads and directed workers doing every kind of job. Some of the Levites served as scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.
While they were bringing out the money that had come into the LORD’s house, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the LORD’s law given through Moses.
Hilkiah told Shaphan the scribe, “I found the book of the law in the LORD’s house!” Then he handed the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan took the book to the king and reported, “Your servants are doing everything you put them in charge of.
They emptied out the money they found in the LORD’s house and handed it to the supervisors and workers.”
Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, “Hilkiah the priest gave me a book.” And Shaphan read from it to the king.
When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
He gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant:

“Go ask the LORD about what’s written in the book we found. Ask for me and for everyone still left in Israel and Judah. The LORD has poured out great anger on us because our ancestors didn’t keep his word and do everything this book says.”

So Hilkiah and the men the king sent went to Huldah the prophet. She was married to Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, who looked after the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem’s Second Quarter, and they told her why they’d come.
She told them, “Here’s what the LORD, the God of Israel, says. Tell the man who sent you to me:
‘The LORD says, “I’m bringing disaster on this place and its people. Every curse written in the book they read to the king of Judah is coming.
They walked away from me and burned incense to other gods. Everything they made with their own hands provoked me to anger. So my anger is pouring out on this place, and it won’t be put out.”’
But say this to the king of Judah who sent you to ask the LORD. ‘The LORD, the God of Israel, says, “About those words you heard:
Your heart was tender. When you heard God’s words against this place and its people, you humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and cried in front of me. I heard you too,” says the LORD.
“I’ll gather you to your ancestors, and you’ll go to your grave in peace. You won’t see all the disaster I’m bringing on this place and its people.”’” They took the message back to the king.
The king sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem and brought them together.

He went up to the LORD’s house with the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and everyone, great and small. He read aloud every word of the book of the covenant found in the LORD’s house.

The king stood in his place and made a covenant before the LORD. He committed himself to following the LORD, keeping his commands, testimonies, and statutes with his whole heart and soul, and doing what the covenant said in that book.
He had everyone there in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand with him. The people of Jerusalem kept the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

Josiah removed the detestable things from every territory that belonged to the Israelites and made everyone in Israel serve the LORD their God. As long as he lived, they didn’t turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
